description: We are aspiring developers passionate about space exploration, science, and technology. For the Planet X and SPHEREx challenge, we aim to build an interactive web application to explore SPHEREx sky images over time and visualize changes in celestial objects. We welcome teammates interested in web development, Python, astronomy, data analysis, image processing, and UI/UX. Let's turn space data into discovery together!
summary:
What if we could travel through time and witness how the universe changes? COSMOSCOPE makes this possible through an interactive astronomical time machine and scientific discovery platform inspired by NASA's SPHEREx mission.

COSMOSCOPE transforms complex infrared survey archives into an accessible environment where users can explore celestial objects, compare real astronomical observations across different time periods, analyze spectral data, and investigate potential cosmic changes.

Addressing the challenge of exploring the changing infrared universe, COSMOSCOPE combines observations from SPHEREx, 2MASS, WISE, and NEOWISE, creating a multi-mission exploration timeline spanning approximately 27 years (1998–2025).

Its interactive Sky Explorer, Cosmic Time Machine, Discovery Engine, Image Analysis Lab, and Spectral Lab enable users to compare observations, examine brightness variations, explore SPHEREx's 102 spectral channels across 0.75–5.0 µm, and investigate potential anomalies. Interactive dashboards and downloadable evidence reports help turn observations into meaningful scientific investigations.

By bringing multiple astronomical datasets and analysis capabilities together, COSMOSCOPE makes infrared astronomy more accessible and empowers students, researchers, and citizen scientists to explore, investigate, and better understand our ever-changing universe.
details:
COSMOSCOPE makes astronomical data easier to explore and understand through an interactive platform combining sky visualization, multi-epoch comparison, image processing, and spectral analysis.

Key Features:

  1. Sky Explorer: Explore the sky using interactive maps and multiple astronomical survey layers.
  2. Discovery Engine: Identify and rank potential astronomical anomalies and interesting objects.
  3. Cosmic Time Machine: Compare observations from different years using blink, slider, and difference views.
  4. Image Analysis Lab: Perform image processing, image comparison, and brightness analysis.
  5. Spectral Lab: Explore SPHEREx's 102 spectral channels and study infrared signatures.
  6. Multi-Mission Explorer: Compare observations from missions such as SPHEREx, WISE, NEOWISE, and 2MASS.
  7. Research Library: Access additional astronomical information and research references.
  8. Analytics Dashboard: Visualize findings through interactive charts and data summaries.
  9. Evidence Dossier: Generate downloadable reports containing analysis results and data references.
  10. Home and Tutorial: Provides an introduction, guides, and instructions to help users navigate the platform.

How It Works:

  • Explore: Select and explore astronomical objects.
  • Detect: Compare observations across different time periods.
  • Score: Rank potential changes and anomalies.
  • Investigate: Analyze findings and generate research reports.

Technology Stack:

  • Frontend: React, Vite, JavaScript, Tailwind CSS.
  • Backend: Python, FastAPI.
  • Data Processing: Astropy, NumPy, SciPy, OpenCV.
  • Visualization: Aladin Lite, Plotly, Three.js.
  • Database: SQLite.
  • Deployment: Vercel and Render.

Benefits and Impact:

  • Makes complex astronomical data easier to understand and explore.
  • Helps identify potential changes in celestial objects across different observations.
  • Brings data from multiple astronomical surveys into one platform.
  • Provides accessible tools for students, researchers, and citizen scientists.

Future Scope:

We aim to introduce automated discovery alerts, enhanced anomaly detection, improved analysis capabilities, and citizen-science collaboration to expand COSMOSCOPE's research potential.
